docTitle: Why your app gets slower as it grows

slides.title:
Why your app
gets ==slower==
as it grows
slides.sub: Fast with 10 users, slow with 100,000. Often the fix is a *database index*.

slides.title:
Your database
reads *every* row
slides.lede: Look up one order by email. With no index, the database checks all 1,000,000 rows.
slides.takeaway: This is called a *full table scan*.

slides.title:
An index works
like the one at
the back of a book
slides.lede: A sorted list, each entry pointing to where its row lives.

slides.title:
Finding Bob in
a million rows
slides.takeaway: *3 hops* down the tree instead of 1,000,000 row checks.

slides.title:
Adding one is
*one line*
slides.takeaway: Now the database checks the index first, then goes straight to Bob's order.

slides.title:
Check it's
actually used
slides.lede: Put EXPLAIN in front of your query.

panels.verdict: Using your index. (Bitmap Index Scan too.)

slides.tag: Tiny tables may still show Seq Scan. MySQL: ALL = full scan; ref = index.

slides.title:
Don't index
*every* column

rows.head: Slower writes
rows.sub: Every insert updates every index. 1 row + 6 indexes = 7 writes.

rows.head: More storage
rows.sub: Each index is extra data on disk.

rows.head: Tiny tables don't need one
rows.sub: With about 10 rows, the database just scans.

slides.foot: Index the columns you *search, join or sort by*.

slides.title:
Full video
on YouTube
slides.body: Slow lookup? EXPLAIN it, index it, check again.
slides.video: Database Indexes: Why Your App Slows Down as It Grows
slides.ask: Save this for your next slow query.
